prompt: A 19-person observability startup has 52 paying enterprise customers. Teams renew because its incident timeline joins changes across three clouds, enforces their rollback playbooks, and preserves an auditable record; AI incident summaries are one step in that workflow. Sixty-four percent of new accounts arrive through one cloud provider's marketplace, and the product relies on that provider's identity, billing, and event APIs. The provider will raise its revenue share from 8% to 22% in 120 days, restrict historical event access, and has launched a free native AI incident summary. A new open model also matches the startup's summary benchmark but has not been tested on end-to-end incident resolution. Two consultancies independently built exporters against the startup's private API, but no customer is known to have bought because of an exporter. Marketplace cohorts retain better than direct cohorts; the team has not tested whether buyers will follow it outside the marketplace. The CEO wants to declare an open incident-response platform, publish a free SDK, copy the native summary interface, and commit the full acquisition budget to marketplace ads before the fee change. Decide the positioning and platform strategy for the next 90 days.
criteria: Names competing-and-positioning as primary, starts with a primary owner and ordered named-skill handoffs, and keeps interviews, architecture, rollout, channels, and pricing with their specialist owners.

Anchors the comparison in the enterprise incident-resolution job and material status-quo, native, open-model, and workflow alternatives, separating observed facts from inferences rather than treating interface similarity, benchmark parity, or marketplace conversion as whole-product substitution.

Builds the causal advantage chain and tests the cloud incumbent's installed distribution, ability and incentive to bundle or restrict, legacy constraints, and likely response while treating workflow, data, integrations, trust, distribution, and learning-loop durability as evidence questions rather than automatic moats.

Creates a complete external-platform dependency record and treats the two exporters as a builder-loop hypothesis, then runs bounded portability, direct-buyer, alternate-channel, restricted-API, end-to-end model, and voluntary-builder tests before increasing exposure or claiming an ecosystem.

Selects current positioning, advantage, incumbent, transition, platform-exposure, and platform-creation branches and precommits every double-down, diversify, redesign, migrate, and stop outcome with observable conditions, a 90-day date, exposure guardrails, disconfirming signals, preserved options, and next owners.
